html:
Went to the supermarket in the morning, then stayed home all day.

When you’re at home with nothing to do, time loses its edges. The three meals crowd up against each other; you’ve barely digested one before the next is on the table.

The supermarket was packed and already had a festive New Year feel. Right inside the entrance stood an eye-catching array of red underpants. Tradition says you should wear red in your zodiac year to ward off bad luck, and the coming year is the Year of the Dragon; apparently plenty of people were born under it. Past the checkout were stalls selling spring couplets, the red-and-gold paper verses pasted beside front doors at New Year, as if afraid passersby might forget it was coming.

Tuck those big red briefs in, lad; whoever claps, I’ll call him Dad.

I’m writing day three’s entry on day four. And yet my memory of the day before is astonishingly hazy. All I remember is reading more of the Musk biography in the evening; how the rest of the day went, I honestly can’t recall.
